pages.observedContent: Lecture 30 title Reinforcement Learning.
Objectives: foundations, loop components, policies/values and Q-learning application.
Contents: introduction, exploration, models, Q-learning, Gymnasium and code.

Recap contrasts labeled supervised mapping and unlabeled unsupervised regularities; RL uses interaction and evaluative feedback rather than correct-action labels. Third branch is a pedagogical taxonomy, not an exhaustive universal classification.

Teacher-versus-critic table: prescribed labeled guidance versus evaluation, often scarce/delayed feedback and learned intermediate values. Feedback need not always be delayed or sparse; later dense rewards are compatible.

Trial-and-error example and complete loop diagram: actions travel agent to environment; observations, next state s_(t+1) and reward r_(t+1) return. Dog/treat is analogy, not a required formal action-label dataset.
Agent is learner/decision-maker; environment is outside the modeled agent. Mobile robot/maze example. Boundary is a modeling choice.
Action a_t belongs to action set A; four maze directions are discrete, steering angle can be continuous. Arrows lead from agent to environment.
Return arrow carries observations/state information and numerical reward. State is complete situation description; observation can be partial, as next page explicitly names o_t separately.

Loop uses o_t of s_t to choose a_t, yielding s_(t+1), new observation and r_(t+1). Episode/trial runs from start to terminal in the pedagogical episodic setting. Later continuing task is practically truncated.

Deterministic policy pi:S→A; stochastic pi(a|s) action distribution. Sarsa on-policy and Q-learning off-policy. Regardless of exploration strategy is too broad without sufficient data coverage/convergence conditions.

Finite undiscounted return sums T rewards from r_(t+1). Infinite discounted return uses powers gamma^(i−1), with 0≤gamma<1. Gamma=0 is immediate-only; closer to one retains distant weights. Bounded rewards plus discount give convergence; time limit is not the only reason for discounting.
Optimal value max over policies; Q*(s,a) fixes first action then optimal continuation; V*(s)=max_a Q*(s,a). Expected return, not guaranteed realization; optimal actions can tie.

Bellman derivation splits first reward from discounted tail; next-state transition distribution P(s_next|s,a). Expectations should be conditioned on current state/action and optimal continuation, omitted in compact notation.

State/action Bellman forms and bracket labels inspected. Q*=expected immediate reward plus gamma-weighted expectation of max next Q; V* maximizes current action. Greedy optimal policy needs actual Q*, not arbitrary current estimates.

Exploration gathers information; exploitation follows best current estimate. Source calls exploitation highest immediate reward, but Q values encode cumulative return. Excessive exploit can miss better actions; excessive explore sacrifices use of learned behavior, not a universal theorem of failure.

Model-free examples Q-learning/Sarsa versus fully known model dynamic programming with value/policy iteration. Model-based does not generally require perfect prior knowledge or eliminate all exploration; learned models exist. Model-free does not mean no learned Q model.

Q update with eta learning rate, gamma discount, sampled reward plus max estimated next value minus old estimate. Last Q omits hat typographically. Future value remains estimated, not wholly observed; convergence claim needs finite/tabular and sampling/step-size assumptions.

Full pseudocode initializes Q outside episodes, initializes s per episode, epsilon-greedy chooses a, observes r and s_next, updates Q, assigns s=s_next and repeats until terminal. Side box gives exploration-branch epsilon and exploitation-branch 1−epsilon. Random exploration can also select greedy action; terminal bootstrap convention omitted.

Diagram receives current gripper location and target 3D location; Q-learning reaches target, then separate gripper closing is shown. Reachability and grasping success are not guaranteed; subsequent FetchReach code is not a grasping task.

Gymnasium standard environment API: make, reset, step, render; environments and wrappers support comparable experiments. It is not itself the MuJoCo physics engine or a complete RL training algorithm.

MuJoCo models dynamics/contact/gravity for simulation before hardware. Four illustrations: pick/place, navigation, humanoid, object manipulation. Sim-to-real support is not a guarantee of safe or successful transfer.

Notebook shell command !pip install gymnasium-robotics mujoco matplotlib -q. FetchReachDense-v4: 7-DOF robot, 4-component continuous input, dense reward minus Euclidean goal error. Reward is nonpositive, not strictly negative at zero distance. The environment blocks the gripper channel; do not infer grasping.

Imports gymnasium as gym, gymnasium_robotics, numpy as np and pyplot; gym.register_envs(gymnasium_robotics), env=gym.make("FetchReachDense-v4"). Dense means per-step distance reward. Registration does not instantiate every robot model; current compatibility helper may be no-op after import.

NX=NY=NZ=8; BIN_SIZE=0.04; N_ACTIONS=6. Float32 ACTION_MAP rows [+x,−x,+y,−y,+z,−z], fourth component zero. Unit normalized commands are not guaranteed one metre or exactly one bin of achieved motion. Underlying API remains continuous while agent chooses six vectors.

Q=zeros((NX,NY,NZ,N_ACTIONS)); alpha=.1,gamma=.95,epsilon=.5. get_state: err=desired_goal−achieved_goal; tuple(clip(((err+.16)/BIN_SIZE).astype(int),0,7)). Code bins relative error, not absolute position, and has clipping/state aliasing. Training rewards=[],5000 episodes, obs,_=reset(),s,total=get_state(obs),0. Q persists across resets.

Up to 50 iterations; randint(N_ACTIONS) if rand()<epsilon else argmax(Q[s]); step(ACTION_MAP[a]) returns obs,r,terminated,truncated,info. The else includes equality. Source says terminated means won; generic termination can include failure, and FetchReach is continuing, not success-terminated.

s_next=get_state(obs); Q[s][a]+=alpha*(r+gamma*max(Q[s_next])−Q[s][a]); s,total=s_next,total+r; break if terminated or truncated. Update is before stopping and unconditionally bootstraps. Correct for continuing-task time-limit truncation, not arbitrary true terminal state with nonzero next estimate.

Append episodic undiscounted total; epsilon=max(.05,epsilon*.998); every (ep+1)%500==0 print last100 mean and epsilon. Output: 500 −7.06 .184;1000 −6.86 .068;1500 −7.41 .050;2000 −6.77;2500 −6.14;3000 −5.98;3500 −5.24;4000 −4.90;4500 −3.87;5000 −3.37, all latter epsilon .050. Trend is not monotonic.

smoothed=convolve(rewards,ones(50)/50,mode="valid"); figsize(10,4), plot(smoothed), axis labels, title, grid,show. Source graph rises roughly −9 to −3/−4 with oscillations and final dip, not convergence to zero. Plot x is window index 0..4950, not explicitly aligned final episode. Performance curve does not prove optimality.

Suggested grid12 and smaller bins,20000+episodes,deep RL and fourth-channel gripper action. Hard-coded clip upper7/offset.16 must be reviewed when changing grid. Larger table/sample burden; deep networks avoid explicit tabulation but do not eliminate all dimensionality problems. FetchReach ignores gripper channel, so action-only change cannot create grasping.
Summary repeats interaction/reward, greedy action from Q*, model-free/off-policy Q-learning and example. No new premise; qualifications retained.
